revised.summary:
Stagewatch gets a list of playout links instead of its single Patterns link, so it can run several PlayMap nodes and Patterns desks at once. Find lists PlayMap as well as Patterns. Each link follows its peer's clip for the VT countdown and drives its transport. It also cues PlayMap playlist items or Patterns cues from the running order: GO when the item starts, and an opt-in standby when it loads. Every command's receipt and journal row now say what the peer really did: applied, refused in the peer's own words, accepted, unconfirmed, or not sent. Each command that reached the socket leaves exactly one journal row.

Security changes after review:
- Lines that drive another node's air (`playout`, and the existing `patterns`) are refused from another machine over OSC or Companion TCP, which carry no PIN, unless the operator lists that address.
- A line from an AI is always a proposal. When the target node collects Show Bus approvals, the proposal is sent to that node, which runs it under its own rules with the proposer's name.
- The pairing token never leaves this PC in clear, and there is no clear-token tick.
- PlayMap links use pinned TLS and never fall back to plain once a node is pinned.
- HTTP triggers send a secret only to loopback or to a pinned HTTPS server. They do not follow redirects, and no running-order text can change where the secret goes.

Show-safety changes after review:
- A PlayMap standby shows the item's first frame on the air, so standby is off by default and says so. It is only sent to an idle playlist.
- A Patterns standby moves the Patterns operator's own standby, so it is opt-in. At start, Stagewatch sends only `CUE GO <id>` and lets Patterns' fence decide. It never sends a second GO when Patterns asks for one.
- A timed GO across several nodes holds its untimed members until T − rtt/2. It sends one GO to a sync group's leader and reports late starts honestly.
- Only the link feeding the VT can move the running order, once per item.
- Settings keep the old Patterns keys for one release, so rolling back keeps the Patterns link.

Code changes: PlayMap and Patterns need none. PlayMap gets a docs fix and a fence test after round 3. The Show Bus wording goes through the spec-1-3 area's single master edit and its copy units.

Review: 20 issues; 18 accepted, 1 accepted with a corrected mechanism (`GuardOf` is the timecode-chase guard, not a sync-follower refusal), and 1 partly rejected (the existing 9700 Find stays until spec-1-3 retires it). The answers are in §R of /home/user/Stagewatch/docs/ecosystem/playout-links.md.

decisions.decision: Replace the single Patterns link with a list of playout links (IntegrationSettings.PlayoutLinks, at most 8). Names are [a-z0-9-]{1,24}, never an action word and never another integration's context slug. A schema 1→2 migration turns the 2.17 settings into link `patterns`. For one release the legacy patterns* keys are still written as a mirror of that link. Load rule: if playoutLinks is absent, rebuild it from the legacy keys; if the legacy keys differ from the mirror, they win for link `patterns`. Links, the verb, running-order cues and the module's actions are all gated by FeatureGate.AllowsPlayout (Production), and the refusal names the tier.
decisions.why: Patterns and any number of PlayMap nodes can run together. Today, pointing the only link at PlayMap means giving up Patterns (AppSettings.cs:145-152; MainViewModel.Integrations.cs:40-42). The ids link:patterns and clock:patterns survive (MainViewModel.ShowBus.cs:55-66). Rolling back to 2.17 keeps the Patterns link (SettingsStore.cs:169-177 has no upgraders yet). The licence gate matches today's (MainViewModel.Integrations.cs:41,106).
decisions.alternatives: A second fixed PlayMap link: rejected, because it caps the show at one PlayMap. Stopping the legacy keys at once: rejected because of rollback. Keeping the links in a separate file so they survive a rollback: rejected as more model surface than the gain.

decisions.decision: One PlayoutLink class. The peer's kind is observed: the hello gives it at Find, and STATE confirms it (top-level t:'playmap' means PlayMap; no t means Patterns). A kind profile decides the verbs, local refusals, AT support and TLS. While the kind is unknown, go and cue are refused with words.
decisions.why: Mapper StateWriter.cs:77 writes t=playmap and Patterns' STATE has no t. PlayMap speaks Patterns' grammar on purpose (Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md:36), so the only differences are capabilities.
decisions.alternatives: A kind the operator must set: kept only as an override, 'auto' by default.

decisions.decision:
Pairing asks for the nonce and fails closed.
- After HELLO the link sends `@pn NONCE`; this replaces the @hi PING probe.
- `OK @pn` → prove on that nonce.
- A greeting NONCE or an `OK @pn` marks the connection as Show Bus 1.1, and plain AUTH is never sent on it.
- A refused NONCE on a 1.1 connection → prove on the greeting nonce.
- An older desk gets plain AUTH only when the socket's remote address is loopback. Off this PC, nothing is sent and the link says 'update Patterns'. There is no clear-token tick.
- No answer within 5 s → plain AUTH on loopback; otherwise drop and redial with words.
- After 'wrong token', stop proving until the token setting changes.
- CONTEXT, WHOAMI, INDEX and CUE LIST are sent only after pairing.
- Redial backoff: 0.5 s doubling to 5 s, with jitter.
decisions.why: Both peers answer NONCE at any time with the request id and replace the nonce (Patterns ControlService.cs:413-418; Mapper WireSession.cs:259-262). Today's 1.5 s timer sends AUTH to any host and ignores a late NONCE (PatternsLink.cs:279-284,311). With these rules the existing ShowBusTests fake (greeting NONCE, ERR to NONCE; ShowBusTests.cs:239-263) passes unchanged. The Program.cs fake (Program.cs:1283-1318) only needs to answer an unknown verb with ERR, as a real pre-1.1 desk does. The backoff is Show Bus §4 (SHOWBUS.md:78-79), which spec-1-3 hands to this unit.
decisions.alternatives: An operator tick allowing the token in clear to an old desk: dropped after review (fail closed; Patterns has had proofs since round 87). Waiting for the NONCE answer forever: rejected (no bound).

decisions.decision:
PlayMap links use TLS when PlayMap offers it, with no downgrade.
- When the hello has ports.https and tls, the link dials wss://<addr>:<https>/ws with subprotocol playmap.lines.v1.
- The certificate is pinned per node id with TlsPins. A changed certificate gives CERTIFICATE CHANGED until the operator trusts it.
- Once a node id is pinned, its link dials wss only. A hello without TLS turns the link amber; it never falls back to plain TCP.
- 429 at the upgrade: red, 'locked out for a minute'. Close 4401: red, wrong token.
- Patterns stays proof-paired plain TCP, and its link item says so.
decisions.why: PlayMap serves the same line session over TLS (Mapper/docs/wire/companion.md:7-23; HelloService.cs:95-113). The hello is unauthenticated, so the pin is the trust (SHOWBUS §10). TlsPins and the SlidesAgent pattern exist already (Approvals.cs:240-276; SlidesAgent.cs:186-230). Patterns' wire has no TLS (L55).
decisions.alternatives: Falling back to TCP when no TLS hello is heard: rejected because it can be downgraded. STARTTLS on 9697/9941: not built on any peer.

decisions.decision:
Receipts complete from the peer's answer, and every attempt leaves one journal row.
- Each send returns a ticket.
- At most 32 tickets are in flight per link. The 33rd command is refused as not sent, and no ticket is ever evicted.
- Only the link thread or send loop writes the socket.
- At a drop, unwritten tickets complete as 'not sent' and written ones as 'unconfirmed'.
- 30 s of silence → unconfirmed.
- A pre-1.1 desk carries no ids, so its ticket completes at once as 'sent, no receipt'.
- OK → applied; PlayMap stage accepted → accepted; Patterns CUE GO Done → applied, Requested → accepted; Confirm → accepted with 'a person's second GO', and no second GO is ever sent; ERR → refused with the peer's words.
- The 3 s HTTP budget is unchanged. On WS and Companion, a later answer arrives as one follow-up with "final":true, once, within 30 s.
- The journal (JournalKind.Playout) gets exactly one row per command that reached the socket, written when its ticket completes.
- PlayMap's applied OK carries no words, so the effect is Stagewatch's own: 'PlayMap Stage left took PLAYLIST GO …'. The effect is then looked for in STATE: 'seen' or amber 'not seen'.
decisions.why: Today the receipt says accepted and the journal says done on send (MainViewModel.Patterns.cs:64-66,86-88; MainViewModel.Receipts.cs:38). The pending map evicts entries silently and old desks get no ids (PatternsLink.cs:165-171,224-226). Show Bus §4 forbids queueing across a drop (SHOWBUS.md:79-80). PlayMap's OK has no payload on success (CommandRunner.cs:96-115; Endpoints.cs:22).
decisions.alternatives: A receipts endpoint to poll: more surface for little gain. Evicting the oldest ticket: rejected, because it leaves an attempt with no outcome.

decisions.decision:
Refuse locally only on the peer's own published facts.
- Patterns pause/stop: video.pausable and video.stoppable win when present. When absent, role playlist or stinger is refused in Patterns' words.
- PlayMap is never refused by role.
- A GO or CUE on a sync-group playlist of a node whose STATE sync.role is follower is refused, naming the leader.
- WHOAMI's `may` greys menus and turns the link amber, but does not refuse locally; PlayMap's ERR is the refusal.
decisions.why: Patterns refuses these (ShowActions.Content.cs:481-505) and publishes role but no version (CommandRouter.cs:228-260). patterns-playmap-side Round 91 adds pausable/stoppable along with L48, so the field's presence marks a newer Patterns. PlayMap pauses playlist items (VerbCatalog.cs:155-161). A follower takes its leader's anchors (EngineCore.Sync.cs:46-80,193-197; PlaybackLanes.cs:173-178), so a GO sent there is overwritten. A WHOAMI read can be stale by up to 5 s.
decisions.alternatives: Relying only on the peer's ERR: kept as the backstop. A version check: impossible, because Patterns' STATE carries no version.

decisions.decision: Keep the 256 KiB line cap. An over-long STATE keeps its first 256 KiB and is read forward-only for t, id, seq, at, video, playlists, sync, project.index and cuestack. If sync or project.index is cut off, together/AT and INDEX refresh are turned off for that link and it says so. The link shows amber with the STATE size.
decisions.why: The whole PlayMap STATE is about 76 KB: main.json is 13,240 bytes and the 30 non-card fixtures total 75,861 bytes, with the round-3 sections still {}. video is at byte 769 and playlists come right after air. sync (2,891) and project (3,930) come after outputs, media and stage (StateWriter.cs:73-214). Today an over-long line is dropped into a counter nothing reads (PatternsLink.cs:40,274,88-89).
decisions.alternatives: Raising the cap: no measured cause. A PlayMap video topic: Mapper code outside round 3's ownership.

decisions.decision:
Timed GO by measured offset.
- Pick one instant T = now + lead (300 ms, 100–2000).
- A PlayMap member with a sample ≤10 s old and rtt ≤ lead gets AT T + offset, using the lowest-rtt sample among the fresh ones.
- A member without such a sample but with an rtt (Patterns, or a stale PlayMap clock) is held on its link and sent at T − rtt/2. A drop cancels it as 'not sent'.
- If any member has no rtt at all, every member is sent untimed and the receipt says so.
- Members of one PlayMap sync group collapse to a single GO to the leader.
- The result is read from playlists[<id>]. Since PlayMap's position comes from the anchor, the journal says 'scheduled for T (± rtt/2)', and 'started late by X' only when the AT was clamped.
decisions.why: PlayMap's PONG and AT read one wall clock (EngineHost.cs:121; EngineCore.Router.cs:253-276), and a past AT is clamped (:268-271). `video` is only the focused lane (StateWriter.cs:263-270), while playlists[] has state, item and positionMs (:323-384). The estimator keeps no sample times today (Resilience.cs:244-274). Pings go every 2 s, so 8 samples span 16 s.
decisions.alternatives: PlayMap converting AT by its own Stagewatch offset: needs Mapper code. Mixing timed and untimed members unaligned: rejected, because it guarantees about lead-ms of skew.

decisions.decision:
The running order cues playout by id. RundownItem.Playout holds up to 4 cues: link, list, item, label, standby, together. standby is off by default.
- On load, with standby on: PlayMap PLAYLIST CUE only when the playlist is observed idle or ended in STATE ≤3 s old. The option is labelled 'shows its first frame on air'. For Patterns, CUE STANDBY, labelled 'moves the Patterns desk's own standby'.
- On start: PlayMap PLAYLIST GO with AT when together. For Patterns, CUE GO <id> only, so Patterns' fence decides. STANDBY and GO are never sent together.
- The manual `playout cue` has the same idle guard.
- Ids come from INDEX and CUE LIST.
- ShowFile.Sanitize checks the cues. An unknown link or id is amber advice, and the cue is skipped with a journal row.
- Planner and executor live in PlayoutDirector (Timer.Integrations), shared by the desk and the rig.
decisions.why: A cued PlayMap lane is on the air (EngineSources.cs:236-257), and Cue replaces even a playing lane (PlaybackLanes.cs:135-146). CUE STANDBY moves the stack's standby (ShowActions.Cues.cs:37-53), and GO fences on the seen standby (CueStackService.cs:174-198; REMOTE.md:196). The rig has its own item model (Stagewatch.Rig/Program.cs:184-234).
decisions.alternatives: Standby on by default: rejected because it shows on air. Automatic STANDBY+GO for Patterns: rejected because it defeats the fence and hijacks the operator's standby. Hand-written trigger rules: no receipts, no guards.

decisions.decision:
HTTP triggers authenticate only over a channel that keeps the secret.
- Auth kinds: none, playmap, patterns, stagewatch, bearer.
- A secret is attached only to a loopback host, or over https with a pinned certificate (pinned by the hello's node id at that host:port, else addr:<host>:<port>).
- A rule with a secret over http to another machine cannot be saved, and is refused at fire.
- With auth set, the scheme, host and port are fixed text; Expand runs only on the path and query.
- The authenticated client never follows redirects.
- Each rule sends a request id, and the reply's ok/stage/error|msg is read.
- A secret in the query string draws a warning at save and an offer to move it into the profile. It is refused only on a rule that also has a profile, and never at fire for a rule that ran before.
decisions.why: Today's HTTP trigger: Triggers.cs:27 (a default client that follows redirects), :86-92 (show text expands into the target), :131-139 (no header, any 2xx counts as OK). Patterns closed the same plain-HTTP token defect as L53 (Patterns/docs/OPEN.md:51). PlayMap and Patterns serve https on their HTTP ports. Stagewatch documents ?pin= (REMOTE.md:107).
decisions.alternatives: Adding Stagewatch to PlayMap's trusted list: still possible, but it doesn't work for Patterns and doesn't read refusals. Refusing every query secret: rejected because it breaks existing shows.

decisions.decision:
One verb on every transport: `playout [<link>] end|restart|play|pause|stop|seek|cue|go …`, appended as ShowCommandKind.Playout. `patterns …` is unchanged.
- With no link named, clip transport goes to the only enabled link, else the VT link.
- go and cue need a link name whenever more than one link is enabled.
- Every playout action is risk High.
decisions.why: The VT pick moves with whichever clip is running (MainViewModel.Patterns.cs:15-22), so a Companion key with no link name could hit different nodes over time. Classify cannot see the peer, and a PlayMap CUE shows on the air. Stagewatch's rule for new commands: an appended kind, parser verb, help line, risk and context rows.
decisions.alternatives: A raw line passthrough: rejected (the link only sends lines it builds). Risk Review for cue: rejected after review.

decisions.decision:
Who may drive another node's air.
- playout and patterns lines over OSC or Companion TCP are accepted from loopback or from an address in Remote.PlayoutFrom (empty by default), and are otherwise refused with words.
- HTTP, WS and MCP need the PIN or a key as today. With no PIN set, the same address rule applies.
- A line from an AI is always a proposal, even when agents act directly. If the link's node collected §11 approvals in the last 60 s, the proposal targets that node with the link's own line, so it runs there as Approved with the proposer's name. Otherwise it is a desk proposal that runs through the link once a person approves.
decisions.why: OSC and Companion run any parsed verb with no credential (OscServer.cs:110-130; CompanionServer.cs:294-305,404-411; REMOTE.md:29-30; oscBindAll defaults to true, AppSettings.cs:271). Agents act directly when approval is off (MainViewModel.Copilot.cs:207-209; McpEndpoint.cs:133-149). PlayMap holds an assistant's line while armed (ShowPolicy.cs:203-210). Under §11 the target pulls approved lines and runs them under its own checks (Approvals.cs:81-108,135).
decisions.alternatives: A PIN on 9923: a larger change, left to spec-1-3. Refusing AI playout lines outright: rejected, because a proposal keeps the AI useful and a person decides.

decisions.decision: One VT, one move per item: a clip end moves the running order only if that link fed the VT at that moment, its nextOnEnd is on, and no clip end has already moved this item execution (ShowController.Execution).
decisions.why: Each per-link watcher would otherwise call _show.Next(), and two clips ending close together would skip an item (MainViewModel.Patterns.cs:42-62; ShowController.cs:127,225).
decisions.alternatives: One show-level next-on-end setting: equivalent, but the migrated per-link flag is kept.

decisions.decision:
Every reader, named.
- Context items link:<name> and clock:<name> are built from link names only, and the integration loop skips playout links.
- The frame's playout row gains `link` and `node` at its end.
- /api/config and the Companion config line gain playoutLinks.
- The copilot's facts gain each link's kind, pairing, whether it can take AT, and its playlist/item ids or cue ids (≤ 50 each).
- Retiring a removed link reuses the existing supervisor: the view model reconciles the old name with a 'False' signature.
decisions.why: Ids derived from IntegrationStatus names would change with the labels (MainViewModel.ShowBus.cs:55-61; Integrations.cs:101-116). PlayMap reads Stagewatch's playout row (Mapper StagewatchTimer.cs:81) and must be able to tell its own clip. Reconcile already retires a running name whose signature turns false (Supervisor.cs:41-61).
decisions.alternatives: A new supervisor Retire API: unnecessary.

decisions.decision: The Show Bus spec is edited once: this area supplies the words for §2 (kind playmap), §3 (the final follow-up receipt) and §8 (PlayMap row) to spec-1-3's single master edit for Show Bus 1.3. The Patterns, AGMessage and PlayMap copies follow through spec-1-3's units S9, P3, A1 and M1.
decisions.why: SHOWBUS.md:3-6 makes Stagewatch's file the master with copies elsewhere. spec-1-3 owns the master edit and the copy hash rule (design/spec-1-3.md:8-16, decision 10).
decisions.alternatives: Editing the master and the copies here: rejected, because four areas editing one file would chase a moving hash.

decisions.decision:
Review items partly rejected or corrected.
(a) The 9700 Find is not removed here. It is existing code (PatternsLink.cs:420-445), and spec-1-3 decision 11 keeps it until Patterns' L47 walk row (Patterns/docs/OPEN.md:37). This design adds no 9700 code.
(b) The claim that 'followers are guarded, so a GO is refused' is wrong: GuardOf is the timecode-chase guard (PlaybackLanes.cs:302-316; EngineCore.Timecode.cs:208), and PlayMap accepts a GO on a follower. The fix still holds, because the leader's next anchor overwrites that GO: send one GO to the leader and refuse locally on a follower.
decisions.why: Each item was checked against the code. The sibling area owns the 9700 retirement. The sync behaviour comes from EngineCore.Sync.cs:46-80,193-197.
decisions.alternatives: Removing 9700 now: it would contradict spec-1-3 and drop discovery of desks whose 9928 hello has never been walked on a real network.

revised.wire:
STAGEWATCH GRAMMAR (HTTP /api/<verb>/<args…> with X-Request-Id; WS {"cmd","args","id"}; OSC /stagewatch/playout; Companion TCP "@id PLAYOUT …"; MCP run_command)
  playout [<link>] end [<1-3600>]        -> VIDEO END n
  playout [<link>] restart               -> VIDEO RESTART
  playout [<link>] play|pause|stop       -> VIDEO PLAY|PAUSE|STOP (never bare STOP)
  playout [<link>] seek <s|m:ss|h:mm:ss> -> VIDEO SEEK <seconds>
  playout [<link>] cue <playlist> <item> -> PlayMap PLAYLIST CUE <pl> <item> (only to an idle or ended playlist)
  playout [<link>] cue <cue>             -> Patterns CUE STANDBY <cue>
  playout [<link>] go <playlist> [<item>] [together] -> PlayMap PLAYLIST GO <pl> <item> [AT <peer unix ms>]; with no item: PLAYLIST GO <pl> EXPECT <observed next id>
  playout [<link>] go <cue>              -> Patterns CUE GO <cue id> (Patterns' standby fence decides; never STANDBY+GO)
  patterns end|restart|play|pause|stop|seek …   (unchanged; link `patterns`, else the only link)
Targets: with no link named, end/restart/play/pause/stop/seek go to the only enabled link, else the link feeding the VT. go and cue go to the only enabled link, else they are refused ("two playout links — name one: …"). go and cue are refused while the link's kind is unknown.
Link names: [a-z0-9-]{1,24}. Never an action word, never a reserved integration slug (powerpoint, presenter-pcs, vmix, speech, time-server, ltc, ltc-in, cue-lights, triggers, rooms, the assistant's).
Risk: High for every playout action (Copilot.Classify and ShowContext.Commands).
Errors: parse "playout takes end, restart, play, pause, stop, seek, cue or go". Execution: "no playout link called x — links: …"; "Stage left's kind is not known yet — no STATE heard"; "not cued — Show is playing on Stage left; GO will play it"; "Stage right's Show follows sync group main (leader …) — GO its leader"; "playout links need Stagewatch Production".
AUTH: HTTP/WS need the PIN or a control key; MCP needs the PIN or an MCP key; a node key may not run playout. OSC and Companion TCP: playout and patterns lines are accepted from loopback or from an address in remote.playoutFrom (≤ 16), else refused "playout from another machine over OSC/Companion TCP needs its address in Settings → Remote → May drive playout (these carry no PIN)". The same address rule applies to HTTP/WS/MCP when no PIN is set. AI origin (MCP run_command, or a §11 proposal aimed at Stagewatch): always a proposal. If the link's node collected approvals in the last 60 s, the proposal goes to POST /api/proposals-equivalent internal SubmitLocal with from {t:"agent",id:"mcp",name:"AI agent (MCP)"}, target {t:<kind>,id:<node id>} and the link's own line (e.g. "PLAYLIST GO pl1a2b3c4 it9f8e7d6"), with risk from the target's context commands.

RECEIPTS (Show Bus §3)
HTTP 200 {"type":"receipt","id":"a1","ok":true,"stage":"applied","effect":"PlayMap Stage left took PLAYLIST GO Show · Intro","error":null,"refs":{"peerRequest":17}}
HTTP 409 {"type":"receipt","id":"a1","ok":false,"stage":"applied","effect":"","error":"PlayMap Stage left refused PLAYLIST GO: Show has no item #9","refs":{"peerRequest":17}}
HTTP 409 local refusal: error "Patterns: 'x' is a playlist item — its own clock keeps running, so it is not paused (patterns end, restart or seek move it)"; nothing is sent.
HTTP 409 error "not sent — the link to Stage left dropped" | "32 commands are waiting on Stage left's answers — not sent".
HTTP 200 stage "accepted", effect "sent to PlayMap Stage left — waiting for its answer", refs.peerRequest, when no answer comes within 3 s.
HTTP 200 stage "accepted", effect "Patterns asks for a second GO within 4 s — a person's" (from outcome Confirm; Stagewatch never sends the second GO).
HTTP 200 stage "accepted", effect "sent — this desk gives no receipts (older than Show Bus 1.1)".
WS follow-up, at most once within 30 s, only after an accepted receipt that waits on a peer: {"type":"receipt","id":"a1",…,"final":true}. "final" is a new last field, written only on follow-ups. When nothing comes back: effect "unconfirmed — no answer in 30 s" or "unconfirmed — the link dropped before it answered".
Companion: "OK @c1 accepted sent to …", then "OK @c1 applied …" or "ERROR @c1 PlayMap Stage left refused …".
Peer answer mapping:
- OK @id → applied.
- OK @id {"stage":"accepted"} (PlayMap) → accepted.
- Patterns {"outcome":"Done"} → applied; "Requested" → accepted; "Confirm" → accepted with the person's-second-GO words.
- ERR @id words → refused.
Bounds: at most 32 tickets in flight per link, none evicted. The queue is emptied at a drop ("not sent").

STAGEWATCH → PEER (line wire per link: TCP to Patterns 9697 / PlayMap 9941, or wss://<addr>:<https>/ws with subprotocol playmap.lines.v1 for PlayMap with tls or a pinned node id)
  HELLO Stagewatch   (PlayMap answers OK)
  @pn NONCE → OK @pn <hex> | ERR … (pre-1.1 desk) | no answer in 5 s (fail closed: loopback → plain AUTH; otherwise drop and redial with words)
  @pa AUTH-PROOF <lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256(token upper-cased without dashes/spaces, nonce+"Stagewatch")> → OK @pa paired | OK @pa open — … | ERR @pa wrong token (no more proofs until the token setting changes)
  The proof uses the answered nonce. After a greeting NONCE or an OK @pn, plain AUTH is never sent on that connection. A refused NONCE on a 1.1 connection proves on the greeting nonce.
  AUTH <token> — only to a pre-1.1 desk, only when the socket's remote address is loopback.
  PING <unix ms> → OK PONG t1 t2 t3 (every 2 s)
  After pairing: @ctx CONTEXT (every 5 s); @wh WHOAMI (PlayMap, every 5 s and when show.armed moves); @ix INDEX (PlayMap, when project.index moves); @cl CUE LIST (Patterns, when cuestack.listRev moves)
  @s<n> VIDEO END <s>|VIDEO RESTART|VIDEO PLAY|VIDEO PAUSE|VIDEO STOP|VIDEO SEEK <s>
  @s<n> PLAYLIST CUE <pl-id> <item-id>
  @s<n> PLAYLIST GO <pl-id> <item-id> [AT <T_local + offset_ms>]   (for an untimed member of a together set: written at T − rtt/2)
  @s<n> CUE STANDBY <cue-id> (manual, or on load when opted in)
  @s<n> CUE GO <cue-id>
  Redial backoff 0.5 s doubling to 5 s, with jitter.
  Over wss: no Origin, Host = the address, one text frame per line, inbound frames capped at 256 KiB, the greeting STATE after OK paired. 429 at the upgrade = locked out (red). Close 4401 = wrong proofs (red). A pinned node id is never dialled plain.
  Read from the peer, forward-only:
  - STATE: t, id, seq, at;
    video{file,role,tag,key,positionMs,lengthMs,paused,rate,seq,pausable?,stoppable?};
    playlists[{id,name,state,item{id,label},positionMs,syncGroup,next{id}}];
    sync{role,leader}; project.index;
    cuestack{armed,hold,listRev,standby{id,requireConfirm}}.
    Over 256 KiB, only the prefix is read.
  - WHOAMI: paired, role, armed, may.

SETTINGS JSON (schema 2)
integrations.playoutLinks[{name,enabled,kind:auto|patterns|playmap,host,port,token:<DPAPI b64>,node,transport:auto|tcp|wss,followVt,nextOnEnd}], integrations.playoutLeadMs (300, range 100–2000). The legacy patterns, patternsHost, patternsPort, patternsToken and patternsNextOnEnd keys are still written for one release as a mirror of link `patterns`; legacy keys that differ from the mirror win. remote.playoutFrom: [address…].
RUNDOWN ITEM: playout:[{link,list,item,label,standby:false,together}] (≤ 4). ShowFile.Sanitize: ids [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}; label ≤ 80 characters with no control characters.
TRIGGER: auth:{kind:none|playmap|patterns|stagewatch|bearer, secret:<DPAPI b64>}.

issues.issue: The design says `Auth is unchanged: the PIN or a control key`. That is false for two transports. OSC and Companion TCP run the shared grammar with no authentication at all. A new `playout` verb therefore turns Stagewatch into an unauthenticated relay into PlayMap's and Patterns' proof-paired sessions. Any host on the LAN could send PLAYLIST GO / PLAYLIST CUE / CUE GO (with AT) that PlayMap and Patterns would themselves refuse without a token. This is a confused deputy: a peer acting as Stagewatch.
issues.evidence: Stagewatch/src/Timer.Remote/OscServer.cs:107-130 (Dispatch → ShowCommandParser.TryParse → _control.Execute, no auth check). AppSettings.cs:269-271 (oscBindAll defaults to true). CompanionServer.cs:40-44 (bindAll) and :293-300 (any shared verb runs). docs/REMOTE.md:29-30 lists OSC and Companion TCP auth as "none". PlayMap requires a token, proof or trusted address before transport: Mapper WireSession.cs:76-86 and ShowPolicy.cs:31 (an unpaired session is Observer).
issues.fix: Refuse `playout` (and, for consistency, `patterns`) on OSC and on Companion TCP from non-loopback senders. Allow it only through an explicit per-transport allow list or a key. Say this in REMOTE.md, COMPANION.md and the context `commands` rows. Add a test showing that OSC `/stagewatch/playout x go …` from the LAN is refused and the fake peer hears nothing.

issues.issue: HTTP trigger auth sends X-PlayMap-Token or X-Patterns-Token over plain http://, and the design's own example target is http://10.0.0.12:9940. That puts the pairing token in clear on the LAN, which contradicts the design's G08 aim. Patterns treated exactly this as a defect (L53) and closed it with TLS. Two more ways the secret can leak: the target URL is expanded with {TITLE} and {DETAIL}, so running-order text can steer where the secret goes; and HttpClient follows redirects, which keeps custom headers.
issues.evidence: Triggers.cs:129-135 (`var url = Expand(r.Target, ctx)`, default HttpClient). Patterns/docs/OPEN.md:51 (L53: "the token rode as the X-Patterns-Token header over plain HTTP", closed in 88.3/88.4 by TLS). Patterns/docs/REMOTE.md:602-604 (HTTPS on the same control port). Mapper hello carries ports.https and tls (HelloService.cs:109-113).
issues.fix: Attach a secret only to loopback, or to https:// pinned with TlsPins by the target's hello node id (the same rule as the link). Forbid placeholders in scheme, host and port when auth is set. Set AllowAutoRedirect=false on the authenticated client. Refuse to save a rule that sends a secret to plain http on a non-loopback host.

issues.issue: PlayMap standby is not air-safe, so the claim that `standby never cuts the air` is wrong. A cued item is on the air: PLAYLIST CUE on an idle playlist puts that item's held first frame on its outputs. On a playing playlist it replaces the lane unconditionally, which cuts the picture. The planner sends CUE when an item loads, which can be minutes before GO. The manual `playout cue` verb has no observed-playing guard, yet its risk is Review, which the copilot pre-ticks.
issues.evidence: Mapper/src/PlayMap.Engine/Rendering/EngineSources.cs:247-257 ("…or the frame's own instant while the item is cued and has not started"; Item() returns null only for idle lanes, :240). PlaybackLanes.cs:135-146 (Cue overwrites `_lanes[list.Id]` with no playing check). Copilot.cs:16-19 (Review = ticked by default; High = changes what the audience sees). Design §1.9 and §2.1.
issues.fix: Make PlayMap standby opt-in per cue, labelled "shows its first frame on air at load", and off by default. Apply the observed-playing guard to the manual `playout cue` as well, refusing with words. Classify `playout cue` as High (Classify cannot see the peer kind), or make it kind-aware.

issues.issue: The existing link tests cannot move with their assertions unchanged, and the pairing rule has a hole. (1) The ShowBusTests fake answers `ERR @pn unknown word` to NONCE. Under the design that means 'old desk', so on loopback plain AUTH is sent, which breaks the assertion that the token never crosses the wire. (2) The Program.cs fake never answers `@pn NONCE`. Under 'never time it' the link waits forever, so `HELLO then AUTH` fails. (3) A peer that has already sent a greeting NONCE is 1.1 by definition and must never be sent plain AUTH. The design treats that NONCE only as a hint.
issues.evidence: tests/Stagewatch.Tests/ShowBusTests.cs:241-263 (greeting NONCE, then `ERR {id}unknown word` for anything else; asserts no `AUTH ` line). Program.cs:1283-1318 (the reader answers only lines starting with PING; asserts `AUTH s3cret`). PatternsLink.cs:279-284 (today's timer fallback that this replaces).
issues.fix: Rule: after a greeting NONCE, never plain AUTH. If the NONCE verb is refused, prove on the greeting nonce. If NONCE gets no answer within a bounded wait, fail closed with words rather than wait forever. Update the fakes to implement the NONCE verb, and say in the papers that the tests changed.

issues.issue: An AI can escalate its privileges through the link. With AgentsNeedApproval off, MCP agents act directly. A `playout … go` from an agent then reaches PlayMap as Stagewatch's Remote role. PlayMap's own policy would hold an assistant's transport line for a person while armed. Peer proposals approved through §11 also lose their proposer identity on PlayMap.
issues.evidence: Stagewatch MainViewModel.Copilot.cs:207-209 (returns null, so the command runs directly, when !AgentsNeedApproval). McpEndpoint.cs:142-149. Mapper ShowPolicy.cs:203-210 (Assistant → Propose while armed). Mapper/docs/SHOWBUS-NODE.md §2 (approvals already reach PlayMap and run under its own checks).
issues.fix: Always propose `playout` lines that come from an AI or a peer, even when agents act directly. Better: route them as §11 proposals targeted at the PlayMap node, so they run as role Approved with the proposer's name.

issues.issue: The outbound queue and journal-on-answer can turn attempts into silent facts. Show Bus §4 says nothing is queued while a link is down, but lines still in the outbound queue at a drop would be reported 'accepted/unconfirmed' instead of 'not sent'. The existing pending map evicts entries above 64 silently, so their tickets never complete. Pre-1.1 desks get no request ids, so no answer can ever be matched. In all three cases a command leaves no journal row at all, which is worse than today's journal-on-send.
issues.evidence: SHOWBUS.md §4 ("never queues commands while a link is down: a command to a dead link fails at once"). PatternsLink.cs:165-171 (ids only when _bus11; eviction at :169). PatternsLink.cs:224-226 (drop completes only pending entries).
issues.fix: Clear the queue on disconnect and complete its tickets as refused "not sent — the link dropped". Complete evicted tickets as 'unconfirmed'. Journal 'sent, no answer' after the deadline, including for id-less old desks. Test each case.

issues.issue: The timed GO is weaker than claimed. (a) A stale clock or a Patterns peer means some links are sent untimed while others get AT T+offset. That guarantees roughly lead-ms (300 ms) between nodes, worse than all untimed. (b) It ignores PlayMap's own sync groups: followers are guarded, so a GO sent to one is refused, and leader time already gives frame-accurate sync. (c) Taking the best of 8 samples and then requiring it to be ≤10 s old is often stale, because 8 pings at 2 s span 16 s.
issues.evidence: Mapper PlaybackLanes.cs:138,152 (GuardOf) and :174 (sync-group followers adopt the leader). StateWriter.cs:361-364 (playlists[].syncGroup). Stagewatch Resilience.cs:244-274 (window 8, no sample time stored). PatternsLink.cs:43 (PING every 2 s).
issues.fix: When a 'together' set contains an untimed member, hold its send locally until T − rtt/2, or send every member untimed. Send one GO to the leader of a PlayMap sync group. Choose the best sample among those that are ≤10 s old.

issues.issue: The 'observed start' is not an observation. PlayMap's positionMs comes from the transport anchor, so `at − positionMs` simply echoes the AT instant; it only catches a late, clamped start. `video` is the focused playlist only, so the GO'd playlist may not be in it. The 'started 4 ms off' wording ignores the offset's ±rtt/2 error.
issues.evidence: Mapper StateWriter.cs:262-270 (video = Focused lane) and :350-351 (positionMs = PositionAt(now) − InNs, anchor maths). EngineCore.Router.cs:265-270 (AT is clamped with Math.Max(0, delta)). Mapper fixtures observe.json and showing.json are still `{}` placeholders (README).
issues.fix: Read playlists[<id>] rather than video. Report 'scheduled for T (±rtt/2)' and 'started late by X' only when clamped. Name the real observed start as waiting on PlayMap's round-3 observer, in what the round did not do.

issues.issue: With no link named, a high-risk command's target comes from moving state, which is not fail-closed. 'Else the VT link' depends on which clip is running, so the same Companion `playout go …` key can hit different nodes over time. The argument grammar (`cue <pl> <item>` vs `cue <cue>`) also depends on a kind that is unknown until the first STATE arrives.
issues.evidence: MainViewModel.Patterns.cs:15-22 (PickPlayout prefers whichever source is running). Design §1.11 and §1.2 (kind observed from STATE).
issues.fix: Fall back to the VT link only for clip transport (end, restart, play, pause, stop, seek). Require a link name for go and cue whenever more than one link is enabled. Refuse while the link's kind is unknown.

issues.issue: Patterns standby interferes with the Patterns operator. `CUE STANDBY` moves the Patterns caller's own standby, so the next GO from their desk fires the cue Stagewatch chose. STANDBY followed by GO <id> deliberately defeats the stale-standby fence. Mapping the 'Confirm' outcome to 'accepted' leaves a 4 s window open for anyone's GO.
issues.evidence: Patterns ShowActions.Cues.cs:37-53 (StandbyMove and Standby on the caller's stack). CueStackService.cs:180-198 (GoGate fence on seenStandbyId; Confirm). CommandRouter.cs:149-155 (outcome Confirm, Done, Requested).
issues.fix: Make Patterns standby on item load opt-in per cue. Show a distinct receipt for Confirm ("Patterns asks for a second GO within 4 s — a person's") and never send a second GO automatically. Say in Help that Stagewatch moves the caller's standby.

issues.issue: With one clip-end watcher per link and per-link nextOnEnd, two clips ending close together can call `_show.Next()` twice and skip an item.
issues.evidence: MainViewModel.Patterns.cs:42-62 (WatchClipEnd calls _show.Next() when PatternsNextOnEnd and the live item is a video).
issues.fix: Only the link feeding the VT countdown may move the running order, and at most once per item execution (ShowController.Execution).

issues.issue: The settings migration breaks rollback. Old patterns* keys are no longer written, so going back to 2.17 after 2.18 saves loses the Patterns link. Show files are also an input boundary for RundownItem.Playout, but ShowFile.Sanitize is not in the change list.

issues.fix: Keep writing the legacy keys, mirroring the link named `patterns`, for one release. Sanitise playout cues in ShowFile.Sanitize: at most 4, valid link names, id shapes, labels capped. Unknown links become amber advice.

issues.issue: Refusing trigger URLs whose query contains token, key, pin or secret will break existing shows when they upgrade. Stagewatch's own HTTP API documents `?pin=`, so multi-room triggers to another Stagewatch are legitimate, and `key` is a common harmless parameter name.
issues.evidence: Stagewatch/docs/REMOTE.md:107 ("with the PIN as `?pin=` or an X-Stagewatch-Pin header").
issues.fix: Warn when saving and offer to move the secret into the auth profile. Refuse only for new rules, or for rules that also carry an auth profile. Never refuse at fire time a rule that worked before.

issues.issue: SHOWBUS.md is the master copy, and Patterns and AGMessage each keep a copy. Adding a §3 'final' follow-up receipt and the §2/§8 PlayMap rows makes those copies drift. Updating Patterns' copy is a Patterns round with its papers, which contradicts the design's 'Patterns: none'. A new receipt shape is also a contract change, which raises whether the spec version must bump.

issues.fix: Land the spec edits through the spec-1-3 area as one owner, with the version decided there. List the Patterns and AGMessage copy updates as their own units: for Patterns, a round with PLAN, REVIEW, CHANGELOG and OPEN, and no walk needed.

issues.issue: The choice between TLS and plain TCP comes from an unauthenticated UDP hello, so it can be downgraded. Someone who suppresses or spoofs the hello moves a PlayMap link from pinned wss to plain TCP 9941.
issues.evidence: SHOWBUS.md §10 ("The hello is unauthenticated, so the pin — not the hello — is the trust"). Design §1.4 (transport auto).
issues.fix: Once a node id has a pin, its link uses wss only, and a missing TLS hello is shown amber rather than silently falling back to TCP.

issues.issue: Context ids can collide, or change. Link names are not reserved against existing `link:` ids such as vmix, triggers, rooms, ltc, cue-lights or time-server. LinkItems also builds ids from IntegrationStatus names, so per-link rows named by label would produce link:patterns-foh, not link:patterns.
